# Seneca quote sources

14 passages attributed to Seneca in this archive, each with the locator that lets you find it in the work itself — and the one thing that most often goes wrong when people quote Seneca.

[Quote source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) / Seneca

How to cite this author, and what circulates under the name that is not theirs to give.

## Sourcing profile

Language of the works

Latin

Cited here from

The Letters to Lucilius (Epistulae Morales), cited by letter and section, and one passage from the tragedy Hercules Furens.

How to cite it

Letter and section — Ep. 1.1–3, Ep. 107.11 — because the letters are short and a bare letter number can point at a passage of several paragraphs. Cite the tragedy by verse number instead; it is a different work in a different genre.

Where quotations of this author go wrong

Two of the letters in this archive quote earlier authors by name, Cleanthes and Hecato, and Seneca says so himself. A line whose value comes from its being inside a letter of Seneca is not the same as a line Seneca wrote, and lumping the two together credits him with sentences he was passing on.

1 of the passages below have been worked through against the cited edition, with the original-language wording and the circulating variants recorded on their own pages.

## Frequently asked questions

### Where can I check quotations attributed to Seneca?

Letter and section — Ep. 1.1–3, Ep. 107.11 — because the letters are short and a bare letter number can point at a passage of several paragraphs. Cite the tragedy by verse number instead; it is a different work in a different genre. This archive cites Seneca from The Letters to Lucilius (Epistulae Morales), cited by letter and section, and one passage from the tragedy Hercules Furens. Every passage listed on this page carries that locator, so it can be found in any edition of the work.

### What is the most common mistake when quoting Seneca?

Two of the letters in this archive quote earlier authors by name, Cleanthes and Hecato, and Seneca says so himself. A line whose value comes from its being inside a letter of Seneca is not the same as a line Seneca wrote, and lumping the two together credits him with sentences he was passing on.

### What language did Seneca write in?

Latin. Any English sentence you read is a translation, so a complete source names the translator as well as the passage.
